issue: PMAT-234 — gate R's verdict line said the opposite of the truth after every successful release. scripts/dogfood/release-check.sh kept ONE flat `pending` string and read it as 'the tag is not cut yet'. Arm 6 adds a note after every successful release (Cargo.toml is back at the newest tag's version, so no cut is in flight and no crux document is owed), so on main the gate printed `PASS pre-tag: 19 PR(s) since v1.27.0 … PENDING until the tag is cut: no docs/audits/crux-1.28.0.md …` about a version that was tagged, released, on crates.io and rendered on docs.rs. The notes are two sets now — note_pretag for the arms whose obligation does not exist until the tag does, note_pending for everything else — and either verdict reports the other set as `also pending` rather than dropping it. Two of three review lanes then found a second false statement in the one remaining note: it asserted the crux document was MISSING, and it is present and 13,860 bytes.
recorded_at: after the round, the refutation, and the re-run that reproduced it on the live repository

quorum.rounds: one round of three sandboxed agy quorum lanes on a517c9af with the base pinned and --not-before set to the dispatch instant. All three returned, exits 0/0/0, durations 371s/332s/333s. Verdicts 1 PASS, 2 FAIL — recorded as it fell rather than resolved by majority, because what decides it is that the refutation reproduces.
quorum.kill_rule: the brief fixed the ORDER of the attack: enumerate every note_ call site and assign its bucket; look for a state where the old script exited non-zero and the new one exits 0; look for a state where `also pending` drops a note or sits beside a false `CRUX present`; rebuild the harness in the lane's OWN temp dir and watch the published case go red on origin/main; diff the moved fixture for behaviour rather than formatting; check the cargo search output shape against the real tool. All six produced a confirmation — and the finding that mattered came from OUTSIDE the list, which is the value of an adversarial round over a self-review: the brief could not ask about a defect its author had not noticed, and two lanes noticed it anyway.
refuted_claims: That the one remaining note says something true — it asserted the crux document was MISSING, and docs/audits/crux-1.28.0.md is present and 13,860 bytes. Refuted 2/3, unasked, re-run before it was accepted. The note now reports the document's state as a measurement in both directions, and a fourth case drives both.
lane_errors: The delegate stopped at its 30-turn limit while summarising, AFTER all three lanes had completed and reduce.json was written. The lane JSON was read directly rather than resuming for a summary of output already on disk. Second occurrence in this session at exactly that point.

One lane returned PASS on a diff two others refuted. Its six confirmations agree with theirs; it simply did not look at the note's wording, which the brief had not asked about. Recorded rather than averaged away.

Both in docs/audits/logs/PMAT-234-pretag.log.

crux.verdict: accept(a tool's single summary line is the only line an operator is told to read, and every surveyed system treats a status summary as load-bearing rather than decorative — `terraform plan`'s counts, `ansible-playbook`'s PLAY RECAP, `kubectl rollout status`. None of them has a state in which the summary asserts the opposite of the resource's actual condition. A gate whose verdict line is wrong is worse than one with no verdict line, because the false line stops anybody looking.)
